STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r6.speaker: Āl, IJ
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r6.claim: Other authorities also classify verses 95–97 and 112 as Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r6.anchor: Others also consider vv. 95–97 (Āl, IJ) and v. 112 (IJ) to be Madinan verses.

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r18.claim: Believers are instructed to fulfill God's pact and keep their oaths to others.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r18.anchor: instructs believers regarding the importance of fulfilling the pact of God and keeping their oaths to others (vv. 91–96)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Those who persevere in truth despite opposition are promised the best reward in this world and the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: People who persevere on the truth in spite of opposition from their rivals are promised best reward both in this world and in the next.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sūrah answers objections raised to create doubts about the Qur’an and the Prophet among the masses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: objections which people were raising to create doubts in the minds of the masses against the Qur’ān and the Prophet (sws) are answered.

TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.claim: The Qur’an contrasts what perishes with what endures, teaching that what is with God is better and lasting.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#25/r2.anchor: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p585/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p585/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p585/r6.claim: Nafida means that a thing ran out or was exhausted.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says worldly things pass away while what God has is everlasting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r13.anchor: فإن هذه هي التي عهد الله إلى عباده فيها وبين تعالى الفرق بين حال الدنيا وحال الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r14.claim: The statement that what God has remains proves Paradise's bliss never ends, opposing Jahm ibn Ṣafwān's claim that it ends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r14.anchor: ودل قوله: وما عند الله باق، على أن نعيم الجنة لا ينقطع، وفي ذلك حجة على جهم بن صفوان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r16.claim: Those who are patient struggle to uphold Islam's covenant, endure unbelievers' harm, avoid sins, and earn only lawfully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r16.anchor: وصبروا: أي جاهدوا أنفسهم على ميثاق الإسلام وأذى الكفار، وترك المعاصي، وكسب المال بالوجه الذي لا يحل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r17.claim: One view says the best deeds are voluntary acts, since people undertake them freely rather than being required to do them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r17.anchor: قيل: من التنفل بالطاعات، وكانت أحسن لأنها لم يحتم فعلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r18.claim: Another view mentions the best deeds to encourage them, though reward covers both good and better actions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r18.anchor: وقيل: ذكر الأحسن ترغيبا في عمله، وإن كانت المجازاة على الحسن والأحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r19.claim: A third view reads al-aḥsan as simply good, without comparative meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r19.anchor: وقيل: الأحسن هنا بمعنى الحسن، فليس أفعل التي للتفضيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r20.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers that the best deed is patience itself, since every duty requires it and it is the root of all obligations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p590#2/r20.anchor: والذي يظهر أن المراد بالأحسن هنا الصبر أي: وليجزين الذين صبروا بصبرهم

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r1.claim: ما عندكم is a subject followed by its predicate, ينفد.

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r2.claim: نفاد means perishing or going away. نفذ with dotted ذ is a different verb from نفِذ ينفَذ.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r2.anchor: والنفاد: الفناء والذهاب يقال: نفذ بكسر العين ينفذ بفتحها نفاذا ونفوذا

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r3.claim: أنفد القوم means their provisions ran out; خصم منافد describes a disputant seeking to exhaust an opponent's argument.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r3.anchor: ويقال: أنفد القوم. فني زادهم، وخصم منافد، لينفد حجة صاحبه

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r4.claim: The stopping point on باق had already been discussed under Sūrat al-Raʿd.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r4.anchor: وقوله " باق " قد تقدم الكلام في الوقف عليه في الرعد

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r5.speaker: ابن كثير، عاصم، ابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim and Ibn Dhakwan read with the first-person plural نون العظمة, shifting from third-person narration to divine first person.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن ذكوان { ولنجزين } بنون العظمة، التفاتا من الغيبة إلى التكلم

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r6.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r6.claim: The remaining readers use yāʾ for third-person narration, returning to God, already named in وما عند الله باق.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r6.anchor: والباقون بياء الغيبة رجوعا إلى اله لتقدم ذكره العزيز في قوله تعالى / { وما عند الله باق }

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r7.claim: أحسن is comparative in its ordinary sense: rewarding the best entails rewarding what is good a fortiori, by implication of agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r7.anchor: إذا جازاهم بالأحسن فلأن يجازيهم بالحسن من باب الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r8.claim: An alternative denies comparative force to avoid implying that reward for the best entails reward for the good; the author calls this concern mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:16:96/r8.anchor: فروا من مفهوم أفعل؛ إذ لا يلزم من المجازاة بالأحسن المجازاة بالحسن. وهو وهم

ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r2.claim: What people possess passes away, whereas what is with God endures.
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r2.anchor: all that is with you is bound to come to an end, whereas that which is with God is everlasting

ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r3.claim: God promises the patient in adversity a reward according to the best of their deeds.
ASAD-NOTES:16:95/r3.anchor: most certainly shall We grant unto those who are patient in adversity their reward in accordance with the best that they ever did

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p864/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p864/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p864/r1.claim: The nearby promise of a good life and full reward supplies glad tidings, so mentioning bushrā suits this context; the grouped wording suits the verse describing the Book as a clarification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p864/r1.anchor: فناسب السياق هنا ذكر (البشرى) في الآية وناسب الجمع في آية التبيان

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Asim read the promise with first-person plural nūn: wa-lanajziyanna.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم: ولنجزين الذين صبروا بالنون

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r2.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the verb with third-person yāʾ: wa-layajziyanna.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: (وليجزين) بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r3.speaker: علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r3.claim: Ali ibn Nasr transmits a nūn reading from Abu Amr, agreeing with Asim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p77#2/r3.anchor: علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو ولنجزين بالنون مثل عاصم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p78/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p78/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p78/r1.claim: The yāʾ fits the preceding statement that what is with God remains; nūn has the same meaning as yāʾ. The following ولنجزينهم is unanimously read with nūn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p78/r1.anchor: حجة الياء: وما عند الله باق

QIRAAT-ER:16:96:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:8#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:8#1/r1.claim: Yz spells bāqī with its yāʾ, unlike the truncated bāqٍ form; the defective ending is made explicit without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:8#1/r1.anchor: Yz, mutawatir: Full spelling with yāʾ (بَاقِي) vs truncated form (بَاقٍ) — orthographic variant

QIRAAT-ER:16:96:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:11#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:11#1/r1.claim: The variant third-person yajziyanna (“He shall recompense”) replaces first-person najziyanna (“We shall recompense”), shifting from direct divine speech to narration about God.
QIRAAT-ER:16:96:11#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: "Third person (yajziyanna = ""He shall recompense"") vs first person (najziyanna = ""We shall recompense

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r1.claim: The statement that what people possess perishes explains why what is with God is better: worldly enjoyment, indeed the whole world, ends however abundant or long-lasting.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r2.claim: نفد with dāl means to run out or perish; نفذ with emphatic dhāl means to pass through, with a different vowel pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r2.anchor: نفد بكسر العين ينفد بفتحها نفادا إذا ذهب وفنى وأما نفذ بالذال المعجمة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r3.claim: What is with God comprises the treasuries of His worldly and otherworldly mercy and does not expire; worldly blessings count among lasting good deeds because they connect to and lead to the afterlife.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Ibn Jubayr that what is with God in both clauses means the reward of the afterlife; some leading authorities chose this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن جبير أن المراد بما عند الله في الموضعين الثواب الأخروي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r5.claim: Using the nominal form بَاقٍ rather than a present-tense verb signals permanence.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r5.anchor: وفي إيثار الاسم على صيغة المضارع من الدلالة على الدوام ما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r6.claim: Alusi uses the verse against Jahm ibn Safwan's claim that the bliss of Paradise ends.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r6.anchor: ورد بالآية على جهم بن صفوان حيث زعم أن نعيم الجنة منقطع

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r7.speaker: عاصم وابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathir read the verb with first-person nūn, shifting from third-person reference to direct divine speech; the other canonical readers use yāʾ without that shift.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r7.anchor: بنون العظمة وهي قراءة عاصم وابن كثير على طريقة الالتفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r8.claim: The reward clause repeats the promise that God's reward is better, with oath-like emphasis to encourage steadfastness in the covenant.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r8.anchor: تكرير للوعد المستفاد من قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r9.claim: Those who were patient are people steadfast in their covenant or enduring persecution by polytheists and the hardships of Islam, including keeping covenants despite threats of breach.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r9.anchor: على العهد أو على أذية المشركين ومشاق الإسلام التي من جملتها الوفاء بالعهود

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r10.claim: أجرهم is the direct object of لنجزين and means their particular reward corresponding to their patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r10.anchor: أي لنعطينهم أجرهم الخاص بهم بمقابلة صبرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the best deed as patience, an inward act needed for every obligation and thus the head of all works; the wording implies an omitted genitive, the reward of their patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r11.anchor: وهو الصبر فإنه من الأعمال القلبية والكلام على حذف مضاف أي لنجزينهم بجزاء صبرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r12.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r12.claim: The genitive superlative emphasizes the reward's excellence, not that only the best of their works is rewarded; this reading encourages them and parallels the wording in 16:89.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225/r12.anchor: إنما أضيف الأحسن إلى ما ذكر للإشعار بكمال حسنه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r1.claim: One reading promises each person, even for the lowest-ranked deed, the great reward otherwise given for the highest; it generously absorbs momentary distress into beautiful patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r1.anchor: لنعطينهم بمقابلة الفرد الأدنى من أعمالهم ما نعطيه بمقابلة الفرد الأعلى منها من الأجر الجزيل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r2.claim: Another parse makes أحسن an adjective of an omitted reward, with the genitive expressing comparison: God rewards them with a reward better than their deeds through multiplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r2.anchor: صفة جزاء محذوفا والإضافة على معنى من التفضيلية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r3.claim: One view takes the best works as obligatory and recommended acts, or acts whose omission is also preferable, such as prohibited and disliked acts; neutral acts receive no reward. Al-Irshad rejects this as constricting mercy while exhorting good works.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r3.anchor: المراد بالأحسن ما ترجح فعله على تركه كالواجبات والمندوبات

ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r4.claim: Another view says the best is voluntary worship because it is chosen rather than imposed; reward for it entails reward for obligatory good works, but Alusi calls this interpretation entirely unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p225#2/r4.anchor: المراد بالأحسن النفل وكان أحسن لأنه لم يحتم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r3.claim: What people possess is the perishing world; what is with God endures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r3.anchor: {ما عندكم ينفد} أي: الدنيا وما فيها يفنى، {وما عند الله باق}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم والباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim read with nūn; others use yāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r4.anchor: {ولنجزين} [قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم بالنون والباقون بالياء]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r5.claim: Those who keep covenants in ease and hardship are rewarded according to their best deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r5.anchor: {الذين صبروا} على الوفاء في السراء والضراء، {أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r6.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet saying love of this world harms the afterlife and love of the afterlife harms this world, so prefer what endures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p41/r6.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من أحب دنياه أضر بآخرته، ومن أحب آخرته أضر بدنياه، فآثروا ما يبقى على ما يفنى"

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r1.claim: What people possess is the transient goods of this world, and it runs out.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r1.anchor: { ما عندكم } من أعراض الدنيا. { ينفد } ينقضي ويفنى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r2.claim: What is with God is the inexhaustible store of His mercy; this explains the prior judgment and proves Paradise’s bliss endures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r2.anchor: { وما عند الله } من خزائن رحمته. { باق } لا ينفد، وهو تعليل للحكم السابق ودليل على أن نعيم أهل الجنة باق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r3.claim: The patient endure deprivation and unbelievers’ harm, or the burdens of religious duties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r3.anchor: على الفاقة وأذى الكفار، أو على مشاق التكاليف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read the verb with nūn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r5.claim: The recompense is for the best of their deeds, such as obligations and recommended acts, or is better than their deeds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:96/r5.anchor: بما يرجح فعله من أعمالهم كالواجبات والمندوبات، أو بجزاء أحسن من أعمالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r7.claim: What people possess is transient worldly goods they naturally pursue; it runs out, distressing the owner when lost or causing anxiety about its loss.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r7.anchor: أي من أعراض الدنيا , وهو الذي تتعاطونه بطباعكم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r8.claim: God's reward endures and will be given to those who remain steadfast in His covenant; this promise also hints at the hardship patience requires.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p308/r8.anchor: أي الذي له الأمر كله من الثواب { باق } فليؤتينكم منه إن ثبتم على عهده

BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r1.speaker: الجماعة، ابن كثير، عاصم
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r1.claim: The majority read ولنجزين with third-person yāʾ, while Ibn Kathir and Asim read it with majestic first-person nūn, a shift to direct divine speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r1.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالياء ونحن - على قراءة ابن كثير وعاصم بالنون التفاتا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r2.claim: Those who patiently fulfill God's pleasing commands and avoid prohibitions receive their reward; God's generosity raises lesser deeds to the level of the best deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r2.anchor: على الوفاء بما يرضيه من الأوامر والنواهي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r3.claim: God rewards according to the best deeds, raising all works to that level and making lesser works equal to the best.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p309/r3.anchor: أخبر بأنه يعمد إلى الأحسن فيرفع الكل إليه ويسوي الأدون به

DURR-FULL:v5p163/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r14.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says what people possess means their wealth, which perishes.
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: ولا تكونوا في نقض العهد

DURR-FULL:v5p163/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r15.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says what remains with God is the everlasting reward of the Hereafter, which never leaves its recipients.
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r15.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: ولا تكونوا في نقض العهد

DURR-FULL:v5p163/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r16.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r16.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the patient receive reward for their best worldly deeds, while God forgives their bad deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p163/r16.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: ولا تكونوا في نقض العهد

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r2.claim: Everything of worldly value, however abundant, perishes, whereas the kinds of mercy stored with God have no end.

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r3.speaker: الجهمية
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r3.claim: Bursevī presents the Jahmiyya as claiming that Paradise’s bliss eventually ends, and invokes this verse against their claim.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r3.anchor: وهو حجة على الجهمية لأنهم يقولون بأن نعيم الجنة يتناهى وينقطع

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r4.claim: God promises a special recompense to those who patiently bear polytheists’ harm and Islam’s hardships, including keeping covenants and poverty.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r4.anchor: على أذية المشركين ومشاق الإسلام التي من جملتها الوفاء بالعهود والفقر

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r5.claim: Calling their works the best signals the completeness of their goodness; the phrase is not a limitation to some lesser reward.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r5.anchor: وإنما أضيف إليه الأحسن للاشعار بكمال حسنه

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r6.claim: Keeping faith and covenants and enduring hardship yield benefits both in this world and the next.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r6.anchor: أن للوفاء بالعهد والثبات على الإيمان والصبر على المشاق ثمرات دنيوية وأخروية

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r8.claim: A scholar recounts joining two ascetics who vowed to eat nothing made by a creature; when he left their cave for Tarsus to teach, one said he had broken the pact and forfeited gifts they received: traversing earth instantly, walking on water, and concealing themselves at will.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r8.anchor: وعن بعض أهل العلم كنت بالمصيصة فإذا برجلين يتكلمان في الخلوة مع الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r9.claim: The tale warns that choosing worldly benefit—even teaching, despite its religious form—can cost divine gifts; a seeker in retreat must shed every name, status, and outward identity.
BURSEVI:v5p58#2/r9.anchor: اختار ما عند الناس فحرم مما عند الله من الكرامات والكفالات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p270#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p270#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p270#3/r5.claim: What God has stored for Muslims includes good in this life and the next; the promised worldly good exceeds the polytheists’ offer, and the afterlife’s good exceeds all else.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p270#3/r5.anchor: و ( ما عند الله ) هو ما ادخره للمسلمين من خير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r2.claim: The contrast between what people possess and what God has is a concluding restatement explaining why God’s promised good is better: His gift endures while human gifts run out.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r2.anchor: وجملة { ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق } تذييل وتعليل لمضمون جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r3.claim: Nafād means depletion or extinction; baqāʾ means not ceasing to exist.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r4.claim: Since God’s provision does not perish, believers should rely on His promised gift for Islam rather than human gifts, however plentiful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r4.anchor: أي ما عند الله لا يفنى فالأجدر الاعتماد على عطاء الله الموعود على الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r5.claim: The line is generalized like a proverb; “what you have” addresses all people and covers what both promisers and promise-recipients possess, though the warned believers hold nothing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r5.anchor: وبقرينة المقابلة بما عند لله ، أي ما عندكم أيها الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r6.claim: Because obedience means forgoing the polytheists’ immediate offer, God promises reward to those who endure patiently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r6.anchor: ولما كان في نهيهم عن أخذ ما يعدهم به المشركون حمل لهم على حرمانن أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r7.claim: The majority read with third-person yāʾ, referring to God as the one who forbids, promises, and rewards obedience.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r8.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن ذكوان عن ابن عمر وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, Ibn Dhakwan (in one narration from Ibn ʿUmar), and Abu Jaʿfar read with the first-person plural of majesty, an iltifāt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r8.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير وعاصم وابن ذكوان عن ابن عمر في إحدى روايتين عنه وأبو جعفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r9.claim: Ajrahum is the second object of yujziyan, construed with the two-object verb meaning “to give.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r9.anchor: و { أجرهم } منصوب على المفعولية الثانية ل ( يجزين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r10.claim: The bāʾ marks cause, and aḥsan is an intensive superlative: the reward is for the especially good deed of remaining Muslim while enduring persecution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r10.anchor: والباء للسببية . و ( أحسن ) صيغة تفضيل مستعملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r11.claim: The promise is emphatic, marked by the oath lām and emphatic nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p271/r11.anchor: وقد أكد الوعد بلام القسم ونون التوكيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r9.claim: Worldly goods expire or their owners pass away from them, whereas the gifts of the afterlife endure forever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r9.anchor: بأن هذه تنفد وتنقضي عن الإنسان، أو ينقضي عنها، ومنن الآخرة باقية دائمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r10.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r10.claim: Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read ‘We will reward’ with nūn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r11.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r11.claim: The remaining readers use yāʾ for ‘He will reward.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r13.claim: Their patience is restraint from desires and endurance of obedience’s hardships, especially resisting the desire to earn money by the prohibited methods just described.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r13.anchor: وصبروا معناه عن الشهوات وعلى مكاره الطاعة وهذه إشارة إلى الصبر عن شهوة كسب المال بالوجوه المذكورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r14.claim: ‘According to the best’ means in proportion to the best of what they used to do.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p418#2/r14.anchor: وقوله بأحسن أي بقدر أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r7.claim: What people possess runs out at a limited, appointed time, whereas God's reward in Paradise endures without end or loss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r7.anchor: أي: يفرغ وينقضي، فإنه إلى أجل معدود محصور مقدر متناه، {وما عند الله باق} أي: وثوابه لكم في الجنة باق لا انقطاع ولا نفاد له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r8.claim: The emphatic lām introduces God's oath that He will repay the patient according to their best deeds and overlook their worse deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p600#2/r8.anchor: قسم من الرب عز وجل (1) متلقى باللام، أنه يجازي الصابرين بأحسن أعمالهم، أي: ويتجاوز عن سيئها.

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb retain the yāʾ when stopping on باق; the other readers drop it at pause, while all read tanwīn in connected speech.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب: وما عند الله باق

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r3.claim: Retaining the yāʾ follows the original form; dropping it at pause is for ease, and connected recitation uses tanwīn without disagreement.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r3.anchor: وإذا وصلوا نونوا من غير خلاف ولا يجوز غيره، فالإثبات على الأصل والحذف للتخفيف.

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r4.claim: These readers use first-person plural, a majestic self-reference by God.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم: ولنجزين الذين صبروا بالنون على الإضافة إلى نفسه تفخيما

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r5.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r5.claim: The others use third-person ya, whose pronoun refers back to God in وما عند الله باق.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r5.anchor: والباقون بالياء ترجع الكناية إلى اسم الله تعالى في قوله: وما عند الله باق.

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r6.claim: نفاد means running out or perishing; the verb أفند describes a group's provisions running out.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r6.anchor: النفاد: الفناء نفد الشيء ينفد نفادا فني، وأنفد القوم: فني زادهم

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r7.claim: The root is also used of disputants who exhaust an opponent's proof and of reciprocal disputation; a cited hadith uses نافدتهم.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r7.anchor: وخصم منافد إذا خاصم حتى نفد حجته، ونافدت الرجل مثل حاكمته، وهو يرجع إلى أن يريد كل واحد منهما إنفاد حجة الآخر

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r8.claim: Bāqī is that whose existence continues, either without interruption or simply as persistent existence; its opposite is what has perished.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r8.anchor: والباقي: هو الموجود المستمر وجوده، وقيل: الموجود عن وجود من غير فصل، وضده الفاني وهو المعدوم

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r9.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r9.claim: Abū al-Qāsim says a thing persists through a distinct attribute of persistence.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r9.anchor: فقيل: يبقى ببقاء، عن أبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r10.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Hāshim say persistence needs no additional attribute; it is simply continued existence.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r10.anchor: وقيل: لا يحتاج إلى معنى به يبقى وإنما هو استمرار الوجود، عن أبي علي، وأبي هاشم

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r11.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r11.claim: Most exegetes say that substance persists.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r11.anchor: واختلفوا في الجوهر، فقيل: يبقى، عن أكثر المفسرين

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r12.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r12.claim: Abū Hāshim says not all substance persists.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r12.anchor: وقيل: لا يبقى كله، عن أبي هاشم

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r13.speaker: الحشوية
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r13.claim: The Ḥashwiyya say all substance persists.

JISHUMI:v6p4105/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r14.speaker: مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r14.claim: The author's teachers say that some substance persists and some does not, with further disagreement over the details.
JISHUMI:v6p4105/r14.anchor: وقيل: بعضه يبقى وبعضه لا يبقى، عن مشايخنا، ثم بينهم اختلاف في تفاصيله.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r1.claim: What people possess consists of transient worldly goods, whereas what God possesses from the stores of His mercy endures without end.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r1.anchor: من أعراض الدنيا { ينفد وما عند الله } من خزائن رحمته { باق } لا بنفد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r2.claim: The verb ولنجزين is read either with nūn or with yāʾ.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r3.claim: The patient are those who endured the polytheists' abuse and the hardships of Islam.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r4.claim: The singular indefinite foot magnifies the danger: if one foot slips from the path of truth after standing firm, many feet slipping is all the more alarming.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p590#3/r4.anchor: لاستعظام أن تزل قدم واحدة عن طريق الحق بعد أن ثبتت عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.claim: What people possess refers to the transient world, while what is with God is the enduring afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r1.anchor: يريد به أن الدنيا فانية , والآخرة باقية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p211#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, acts of obedience end, but their reward remains.

MUQATIL:16:94-97/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:94-97/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:94-97/r3.claim: Wealth people possess perishes, while the reward with God in the Hereafter is lasting; those who persevere in fulfilling covenants receive the best reward and have sins overlooked.

MUQATIL:16:94-97/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:94-97/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:94-97/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about Imru al-Qays ibn Abbas al-Kindi when Abdan ibn Ashra al-Hadrami judged his claim to land and a house.
MUQATIL:16:94-97/r4.anchor: حين حكم عبدان بن أشرع الحضرمي في أرضه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r1.claim: What you have is the world's transient goods; what is with God is His everlasting store of mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r1.anchor: اعراض الدنيا ﴿ ينفد وما عند الله ﴾ من خزائن رحمته ﴿ باق ﴾ لا ينفد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r2.claim: Makkī and ʿĀṣim read the verb with nūn; the other readers use yāʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r3.claim: Those who endured the unbelievers' persecution and Islam's hardships receive their reward according to the best of their deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p269#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ الذين صبروا ﴾ على أذى المشركين ومشاق الاسلام ﴿ أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r2.claim: A gain remains little even if large because it passes away; worldly things perish, while God’s gifts and Garden’s bliss remain for those faithful to their covenants.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r2.anchor: وإنما كان قليلا وإن كثر لأنه مما يزول، فهو على التحقيق قليل، وهو المراد بقوله: «ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق»

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r3.claim: The verse contrasts the perishing state of this world with the lasting state of the afterlife for those who keep their covenant and commitment.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r3.anchor: فبين الفرق بين حال الدنيا وحال الآخرة بأن هذه تنفد وتحول، وما عند الله من مواهب فضله ونعيم جنته ثابت لا يزول

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r4.claim: An unattributed poem says lawful and unlawful wealth both vanish, their sins remain, and piety requires wholesome food and drink.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r4.anchor: المال ينفد حله وحرامه يوما وتبقى في غد آثامه ليس التقي بمتق لإلهه

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r5.claim: A second anonymous poem says even a freely gained world must pass away, like shade that briefly shelters before disappearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r5.anchor: هب الدنيا تساق إليك عفوا أليس مصير ذاك إلى انتقال وما دنياك إلا مثل فيء

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r6.claim: Those who persevere are patient in Islam and obedience and refrain from sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولنجزين الذين صبروا } أي على الإسلام والطاعات وعن المعاصي.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r7.claim: The best deeds are acts of obedience; they are called best because other good actions are merely permissible, and promised reward is for obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r7.anchor: { أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون } أي من الطاعات، وجعلها أحسن لأن ما عداها من الحسن مباح

QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r8.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr read ولنجزين with first-person plural nun of majesty; the other readers use yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:95-96/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن كثير «ولنجزين» بالنون على التعظيم. الباقون بالياء.

RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r6.claim: Sense shows worldly goods end, while reason shows afterlife goods endure; the enduring is better than the finite, making this a decisive proof of the afterlife's superiority.
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r6.anchor: الحس شاهد بأن خيرات الدنيا منقطعة ، والعقل دل على أن خيرات الآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من المنقطع

RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r7.claim: If a worldly blessing is noble, knowing it will end spoils its enjoyment and its loss intensifies grief; if it is base, an enduring good is plainly better.
RAZI-FULL:v20p89/r7.anchor: العلم بأنه سينقطع يجعله منغصا حال حصوله ، وأما حال حصول ذلك الانقطاع فإنها تعظم الحسرة والحزن

RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r1.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r1.claim: Jahm b. Ṣafwān says the bliss of Paradise ends; al-Rāzī treats the verse's statement that what is with God remains as proof against him.
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r1.anchor: وقال جهم بن صفوان : إنه منقطع والآية حجة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r2.claim: Faith binds a believer both to remain steadfast in Islam without reverting and to perform all the obligations and requirements of its law.
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أن يصبر على ذلك الالتزام وأن لا يرجع عنه وأن لا ينقضه بعد ثبوته

RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r3.claim: God encourages steadfastness in Islam by rewarding the patient according to their best deeds; people earn reward for recommended and obligatory acts, not merely permitted acts.
RAZI-FULL:v20p89#2/r3.anchor: يجزيهم على أحسن أعمالهم ، وذلك لأن المؤمن قد يأتي بالمباحثات وبالمندوبات وبالواجبات

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r1.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r1.claim: What people possess of their gnoses and beloved things consists of successive traces and alternating kinds: their entities pass away, although their effects remain.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r1.anchor: ويقال ما منكم من معارفكم ومحابكم آثار متعاقبة ، وأصناف متناوبة

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r2.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r2.claim: God’s mercy, love, and constancy toward people are eternal attributes and everlasting qualities.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r2.anchor: وثباته عليكم فصفات أزلية ونعوت سرمدية

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r3.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r3.claim: Another reading says people’s longing to meet God may vanish, while His own welcome and favor toward them never end.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r3.anchor: ويقال ما عندكم من اشتياقكم إلى لقائنا فمعرض للزوال ، وقابل للانقضاء

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r4.claim: A verse of poetry says that the righteous long greatly to meet God, while God longs even more to meet them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r4.anchor: كما قيل : ألا طال شوق الأبرار إلى لقائي . . . وإني للقائهم لأشد شوقا

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r5.claim: The reward of patience is attaining one’s desired object, though the outcomes of different kinds of patience vary.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r5.anchor: جزاء الصبر الفوز بالطلبة ، والظفر بالبغية

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r6.claim: Those who patiently endure hardship in God’s cause receive immense recompense, as promised in 39:10.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r6.anchor: فمن صبر على مقاساة مشقة في الله . فعوضه وثوابه عظيم من قبل الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r7.claim: Those who restrain desire and avoid a lapse for God’s sake receive the chamber as their reward, as stated in 25:75.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r7.anchor: ومن صبر عن اتباع شهوة لأجل الله ، وعن ارتكاب هفوة مخافة لله

QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r8.claim: Those who remain patient under God’s decree, certain they are under His regard, are met by God’s companionship, as in 2:153.
QUSHAYRI:v2p171/r8.anchor: ومن صبر تحت جريان حكم الله ، متحققا بأنه بمرآة من الله

STUDYQURAN:16:95/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r3.claim: What is with God is better because it lasts, while what people possess in this world comes to an end.
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r3.anchor: That which is with God is better, because it subsists

STUDYQURAN:16:95/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r4.claim: Patience is integral to piety; God is with and loves the patient, who receive abundant reward in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r4.anchor: Patience is considered an integral element of piety

STUDYQURAN:16:95/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r5.claim: Jacob is the Quran's model of patience for bearing Joseph's absence, a virtue the story repeatedly emphasizes and rewards.
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r5.anchor: The Quranic model for patience is Jacob, who patiently bore the absence of his beloved son Joseph

STUDYQURAN:16:95/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r6.claim: Job's patience is implied by his faithful endurance of affliction; like other prophets, he is described as steadfast.
STUDYQURAN:16:95/r6.anchor: the mention of Job’s enduring great affliction with faith

TAB-FULL:v14p349/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r2.claim: All worldly possessions, however plentiful, perish, while the good things God has for those who fulfill His covenant and obey Him endure; one should work for and desire what lasts.
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r2.anchor: وما عند الله لمن أوفى بعهده وأطاعه من الخيرات باق غير فان

TAB-FULL:v14p349/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r3.claim: God rewards those patient in obedience through ease and hardship with the best of their deeds, overlooking worse deeds, and graciously forgives their bad ones.
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r3.anchor: على صبرهم عليها ومسارعتهم في رضاه، بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون من الأعمال دون أسوئها

TAB-FULL:v14p349/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p349/r4.claim: God will also forgive their bad deeds by His grace.

SULAMI:v1p373#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r1.claim: Obedient acts that come from people are transient, while God's recompense for those acts endures forever; the transient cannot equal what lasts.
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما منكم من الطاعات فإنها فانية

SULAMI:v1p373#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r2.claim: Another says human obedience is flawed, whereas God's reward and recompense for it remain forever.
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : طاعاتكم مدخولة وجزائي وثوابي على طاعاتكم

SULAMI:v1p373#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says human attributes perish while spiritual states endure; the servant must relinquish self-attributes and abide with God, since what comes from God remains.

SULAMI:v1p373#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r4.claim: Ja'far identifies what people have as obligatory and supererogatory deeds, and what is with God as His attributes and qualities: originated things perish, while the pre-eternal remains.

SULAMI:v1p373#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r5.claim: Abu Uthman says patience is rewarded by God's granting the servant contentment; one who truly follows the path of the patient receives the best reward in this life and the next.
SULAMI:v1p373#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : جزاء الصبر هو أن يعطي الله تعالى العبد رضا

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r1.claim: This statement explains the previous verse’s claim that what is with God is better: worldly, material goods pass away, while what God promises the pious endures, and reason judges the enduring better.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r1.anchor: والباقى خير من النافد بصريح حكم العقل

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r2.claim: The absolute wording states an exceptionless general principle, instantiated by many truths.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r2.anchor: قاعدة كلية غير منقوضة باستثناء، تحتها جزئيات كثيرة من المعارف الحقيقية

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r3.claim: Because keeping a covenant requires patience against the urge to break it, the discourse shifts from the reward of covenant keepers to the reward of patient believers generally.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r3.anchor: لما كان الوفاء بالعهد مستلزما للصبر على مر مخالفة هوى النفس في نقضه والاسترسال فيما تشتهيه

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r4.claim: The promise covers patience in obedience, abstaining from sin, and enduring affliction, provided the patience is for God and sincerely directed to Him, as the context requires.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r4.anchor: وعد مؤكد على مطلق الصبر سواء كان صبرا على الطاعة أو عن المعصية أو عند المصيبة غير أنه يجب أن يكون صبرا في جنب الله

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r5.claim: The باء in بأحسن marks equivalence or recompense, as in saying I sold this for that.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r5.anchor: الباء للمقابلة كما في قولنا بعت هذا بهذا

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r6.claim: He rejects the proposal that God sorts each person’s good deeds into good and better, rewards only the best, and discards the merely good; the context, reward verses, and divine mercy oppose it.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r6.anchor: وليس المراد بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون الأحسن من أعمالهم في مقابل الحسن منها بأن يميز الله سبحانه بين أعمالهم الحسنة

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r7.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r7.claim: He rejects interpreting the phrase as obligatory and recommended deeds set against permitted acts: permitted acts can be good, but they are unrelated to patience and need not be ranked for this reward.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r7.anchor: وليس المراد به الواجبات والمستحبات من أعمالهم قبال المباحات التي أتوا بها فإنها لا تخلو من حسن كما ذكره آخرون

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r8.claim: Nor does أحسن mean recommended acts: obligatory acts have greater beneficial merit than recommended acts, as legal commands make clear.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن ليس المراد به النوافل بناء على عدم الإلزام فيها فتكون أحسن ما عمل فإن كون الواجب مشتملا من المصلحة الموجبة للحسن على أزيد

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r9.claim: For each kind of deed, God gives the patient person the reward due to its best instance, even when the deed performed was not itself the best instance.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r9.anchor: العمل الذي يأتون به وله في نوعه ما هو حسن وما هو أحسن فالله سبحانه يجزيه من الأجر على ما أتى به ما هو أجر الفرد الأحسن من نوعه

TABATABAI:16:96-97/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r10.claim: Patience warrants reward without auditing each deed’s deficiencies, as 39:10 promises that the patient receive their reward without reckoning.
TABATABAI:16:96-97/r10.anchor: أن لا يناقش في العمل ولا يحاسب ما هو عليه من الخصوصيات المقتضية لخسته ورداءته

TABRISI:16:96/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم وعياش عن أبي عمرو
TABRISI:16:96/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim read with first-person plural nūn; ʿAyyāsh reports this from ʿAmr too.
TABRISI:16:96/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وعاصم ولنجزين بالنون

TABRISI:16:96/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:16:96/r2.claim: Other readers use yāʾ, supported by what is with God enduring; nūn has the same meaning.
TABRISI:16:96/r2.anchor: والباقون بالياء وروى عياش عن أبي عمرو بالنون أيضا

TABRISI:16:96/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96/r3.claim: Nafād means perishing; nafida means something ran out, and anfada describes provisions running out.
TABRISI:16:96/r3.anchor: النفاد الفناء ونفد الشيء ينفد نفادا إذا فني

TABRISI:16:96/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96/r4.claim: Nāfadtu means contending by trying to exhaust an opponent's proof; one report says debaters will outdo you, another transmission has qāftu.
TABRISI:16:96/r4.anchor: ونافدت الرجل مثل حاكمته ومعناه يرجع إلى أن كل واحد من الخصمين

TABRISI:16:96/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96/r5.claim: Bāqī can mean continuously existent or existent without interruption; its opposite ceases to exist after having existed.
TABRISI:16:96/r5.anchor: والباقي هو الموجود المستمر وجوده وقيل الموجود عن وجود من غير فصل

TABRISI:16:96/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r6.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:16:96/r6.claim: Al-Balkhī says an enduring thing remains by a quality called baqāʾ.
TABRISI:16:96/r6.anchor: فقال البلخي إنه يبقى بمعنى هو بقاء

TABRISI:16:96/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r7.speaker: الأكثرون
TABRISI:16:96/r7.claim: Most theologians say no separate attribute is needed; baqāʾ is continuation of existence.
TABRISI:16:96/r7.anchor: وقال الأكثرون لا يحتاج إلى معنى به يبقى والبقاء هو استمرار الوجود

TABRISI:16:96/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96/r12.claim: Mā ʿindakum is subject with yanfadu as predicate, and mā ʿinda Allāh with bāqin; the plural pronoun follows man by sense.
TABRISI:16:96/r12.anchor: وما عندكم مبتدأ وينفد خبره وكذلك ما عند الله باق

TABRISI:16:95-100/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:95-100/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:95-100/r1.claim: After the Messenger recited the covenant verses, Imruʾ al-Qays admitted taking another man's land and offered the land owed plus compensation for its fruit; 16:97 was then revealed about him.
TABRISI:16:95-100/r1.anchor: فلما قرأهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال امرؤ القيس

TABRISI:16:96-100/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96-100/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96-100/r1.claim: God's reward is better because what is with God remains while worldly enjoyment passes away.
TABRISI:16:96-100/r1.anchor: الثواب الذي عند الله يبقى والذي عندكم من نعيم الدنيا يفنى

TABRISI:16:96-100/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96-100/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96-100/r2.claim: Those who persist patiently in obedience and in keeping covenants will receive their reward.
TABRISI:16:96-100/r2.anchor: الذين ثبتوا على الطاعات وعلى الوفاء بالعهود

TABRISI:16:96-100/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96-100/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96-100/r3.claim: The best deeds here are obedience, both obligations and recommended acts; merely permissible acts earn neither reward nor praise.
TABRISI:16:96-100/r3.anchor: فإن أفعال المكلف قد تكون طاعة وقد تكون مباحا لا تقع الجزاء عليه

TABRISI:16:96-100/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:96-100/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:96-100/r4.claim: The wording shows that some good can be better than other good, contrary to the claim that no good is better than good.
TABRISI:16:96-100/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على فساد قول من يقول إنه لا يكون حسن أحسن من حسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r1.claim: What people possess runs out and means the transient world; what is with God is lasting reward and honor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r1.anchor: {ما عندكم ينفد}، أي: يفنى وينقطع، يعني الدنيا، {وما عند الله}، أي: من الثواب والكرامة، {باق}: دائم لا ينقطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the reward never runs out: whatever is taken or eaten is replaced; this refutes those who say Paradise's pleasures will end.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لا ينفد؛ كلما أخذت منه وأكلت منه صار مكانه مثله، فمعنى [لا] (¬3) يفنى هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the patient are those steadfast in their religion and in avoiding what God forbade.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد على دينهم وعما نهاهم الله (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r4.claim: The best deeds mean acts of obedience: permissible good actions deserve no reward, while obedience is the best and earns the promised reward; rewarding by the best deeds entails forgiveness of sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r4.anchor: {بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون} يعني الطاعات، وجعلها أحسن أعمالهم؛ لأن ما عداها من الحسن مباح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r5.claim: The passage warns against false oaths and urges people to fulfill covenants and oaths.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الآيات زجر عن الأيمان الكاذبة فيما كانت، وحث على الوفاء بالعهود والأيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says these verses were revealed about Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAbis al-Kindi and his opponent ʿAydan ibn Ashwaʿ over a parcel of land; as Imruʾ al-Qays prepared to swear, he wept and admitted the other's right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p187#2/r6.anchor: وذكر الكلبي: أن هذه الآيات نزلت في امرئ القيس بن عابس الكندي (¬2)، وفي خصمه عيدان ابن أشوع (¬3)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r2.claim: What people possess in this world perishes, while God's reward and honor remain.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r2.anchor: { ما عندكم ينفد } يفنى وينقطع، يعني: في الدنيا { وما عند الله } من الثواب والكرامة { باق } دائم لا ينقطع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r3.claim: Those patient in faith and avoiding prohibitions are rewarded according to the best of their deeds, their acts of obedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:95-99/r3.anchor: { ولنجزين الذين صبروا } على دينهم وعما نهاهم الله تعالى { أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون } يعني: الطاعات

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r3.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r3.claim: Yahya relates that two men from a delegation of Kindah and Hadramawt disputed over land; the Hadrami accused Imruʾ al-Qays of taking part of his property, but had no formal proof.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r3.anchor: قدم وفد من كندة وحضرموت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فبايعوه على الإسلام ولم يهاجروا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r4.claim: The Prophet asked for proof, then ordered Imruʾ al-Qays to swear; the claimant warned that he was wicked and would swear falsely.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r4.anchor: فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألك بينة بما تزعم؟ فقال: القوم كلهم يعلمون أني صادق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r5.claim: The Prophet warned that whoever takes a Muslim’s property with a false oath will meet God while God is angry with him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r5.anchor: إنه من اقتطع مال رجل مسلم بيمين كاذبة لقي الله وهو عليه ساخط

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r6.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r6.claim: When Imruʾ al-Qays rose to swear, the verses were revealed; al-Ashʿath told him that one verse concerned him and the other his companion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r6.anchor: فقام امرؤ القيس ليحلف، فنزلت هاتان الآيتان:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r7.claim: After the verses were recited to him, Imruʾ al-Qays accepted that his own property would perish while his companion would be rewarded for his deeds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p87/r7.anchor: فقال امرؤ القيس: أما ما عندي فينفد، وأما صاحبي فيجزى بأحسن ما كان يعمل

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:95/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:95/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:95/r2.claim: Verse 96 promises that those who patiently endure hardship will receive a reward better than their deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:95/r2.anchor: Bunun için 96. âyette “Asla kuşkunuz olmasın ki, güçlüklere göğüs gerenlerin ecirlerini, yapmış olduklarının daha da güzeliyle vereceğiz” buyurulmuştur

NAHHAS:v2p407/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p407/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p407/r12.claim: ما عندكم is a subject and ينفد its predicate.
NAHHAS:v2p407/r12.anchor: ^ ( ما عندكم . . . ) ^ [ 96 ] في موضع رفع بالابتداء ^ ( ينفد ) ^ في موضع الخبر

NAHHAS:v2p407/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p407/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p407/r13.claim: وما عند الله باق is another subject-predicate construction.
NAHHAS:v2p407/r13.anchor: ^ ( وما عند الله باق ) ^ ابتداء وخبر . وقد ذكرنا مثل باق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.claim: Baqiyyah can mean permanence: what is with God endures, and what is with people passes away.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r5.anchor: والثاني : الدوام ، ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r2.claim: Mā may be a relative noun meaning ‘that which,’ as in what people possess passing away and what God possesses enduring.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن تكون خبرا بمعنى الذي موصولة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r3.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r3.claim: As a noun, mā can also be interrogative, conditional, or an indefinite noun qualified by what follows.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r3.anchor: والثالث : أن تكون استفهاما . نحو : ما عندك ؟

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says mā and man share an origin: man is used for people, while mā is used for other things.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p563/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : ' ما ' و ' من ' أصلها واحد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r1.claim: Ajr is compensation received under a contract for the use of benefits; to hire someone is to assign a wage for an act.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r1.anchor: الأجر : العوض المأخوذ في العقد على المنافع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r2.claim: Ajr also means setting a bone; ijār is a roof without a surrounding barrier, with plural forms ajājīr and ajājirah, and injār is a variant.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r6.claim: The fourth sense is reward for obedience, promised to those who are patient according to their best deeds.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p112/r6.anchor: والرابع : الثواب على الطاعة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

BURHAN:v4p399/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p399/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p399/r4.claim: In its basic use, ما refers to non-rational things.
BURHAN:v4p399/r4.anchor: واصلها إن تكون لغير العاقل كقوله تعالى ﴿ ما عندكم ينفد ﴾ 4

BURHAN:v4p396/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p396/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p396/r6.claim: Relative ‘mā’ does not change for masculine or feminine, singular, dual, or plural; its referent determines whether it means ‘alladhī’ or ‘allatī.’
BURHAN:v4p396/r6.anchor: فالأول من الستة الاسماء الخبرية وهي الموصولة ويستوي فيها التذكير والتانيث والافراد والتثنية والجمع

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r18.claim: ʿInda Allāh can refer to God's reward, which remains.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r18.anchor: عند الله اي ثواب الله قوله تعالى في سورة النحل وما عند الله باق يعني ثواب الله

DAMGHANI:v1p16/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p16/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p16/r6.claim: Ajr can mean the reward for obedience; the source also glosses the Prophet's reward as thawāb.
DAMGHANI:v1p16/r6.anchor: الأجر الثواب على الطاعة قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

DAMGHANI:v1p75/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r7.claim: Bāqī can mean lasting or enduring, as in what remains with God and what is better and more lasting.
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r7.anchor: البقاء الدوام . قوله تعالى في سورة النحل
